subject: redback spider
title: This Spider Flips Itself Into Its Mate's Fangs on Purpose, and It Pays Off

scenes.text: This spider somersaults straight into his mate's fangs. On purpose.
The Australian redback. The female is big and venomous. The male is a speck beside her.
While mating, he flips over and presses his abdomen onto her fangs. She starts eating him alive.
About 65 percent of males die this way. And it's not a mistake.
Being eaten keeps her busy, so mating lasts longer and he passes on more sperm. She's also likelier to turn away the next male.
He could never outfight her. So he turned his death into more children. The flip is the point.

description:
Male Australian redback spiders somersault onto the female's fangs during mating, and about 65 percent are eaten alive.
Maydianne Andrade's research found the sacrifice pays: a male being consumed mates for longer and transfers more sperm, and females that eat their first mate are more likely to reject later ones, so the dead male fathers more of her offspring.
Is this the worst deal in nature or the smartest? Comment below.
first_comment: Some redback males have found a loophole: they mate with immature females, and those males rarely get eaten. Which bizarre animal mating ritual should we cover next?
